review_scope: Seven fixed legacy assets; no manuscript, production, figure, GPU, or network changes.
classification_rule: Image dimensions and OCR transcripts are metadata/observations, not empirical source truth. Lines, scatter points, AUCs, correlations, accuracies, predictions, and attributions remain quantitative.

assets.caption:
All six masking implementations (columns) on five B-scans (rows) spanning one
volume, drawn with the production samplers. Leftmost column is the unmasked
B-scan. Each predictor target block has its own colour; the green contour is
the anatomy reference. The random, \ArmBest{}, envelope and cover arms place
axis-aligned rectangles; the anatomy arms grow cell-wise targets that follow the
retinal band and therefore change shape from slice to slice. Column headings
carry each arm's own probe epoch, which differs between arms, so the AUCs
printed there are not a matched-epoch comparison and only
Table~\ref{tab:main} should be read that way. Panel headings use the artefact
name \texttt{oracle} for \ArmBest{}.
ocr_text: 5 slices (volume idx 2652) - one colour per predictor block, production samplers
All masking arms on the SAME
assets.classification: Selected mask illustrations plus six empirical AUC annotations; epochs and image-selection indices are metadata.
assets.rationale: Actual OCR reads six AUC/epoch headings. All six displayed four-decimal AUCs agree with the retained original-precision inventory rows, but this does not verify the colored target masks, sampler provenance, selected volume, or seed. The whole asset is not nonquantitative.
assets.limitations: No historical mask coordinates, seed/selection receipt, or exact producer was recovered. OCR is fallible. AUC source agreement is an annotation check, not mathematical verification of the image grid. Unequal epochs cannot establish a policy comparison.
assets.unresolved_scientific_claim: Whether the displayed historical target masks were actually produced by the stated production samplers and faithfully instantiate the named policies.
assets.minimal_action: Prefer removing this redundant appendix grid and referring to the already independently reviewed delivered-mask figure. Alternatively retain only the existing mask-image panels without AUC annotations, explicitly label them selected historical illustrations with unrecovered draw provenance, and review the new exact asset/caption. Do not replace these fine-grained examples with invented masks or call the current whole asset illustrative-only.

assets.caption:
Downstream AUC at matched epoch 50 against mask purity, the fraction of
masked patches lying on retinal tissue. The policy whose masks are $97\%$
on-tissue does not separate from the null, while policies at $40$--$43\%$ purity
gain the most. The ordering does not support the intuition that more accurate
anatomical masking yields better representations. The AUC axis is truncated and
no interval is drawn, and the dashed line is
a least-squares fit through the arms shown; with four to five arms this is
descriptive, not inferential. The point labelled \texttt{oracle} is
\ArmBest{}.
ocr_text: The precision paradox: masking anatomy more accurately does not help
assets.classification: Quantitative AUC-versus-purity scatter with fitted and null-reference lines; not an illustration.
assets.rationale: PDF vector tick labels and coordinates independently recover five data points; PNG spines and colored-marker centers agree with the PDF geometry. All five purity values fail the current Table2 geometry source even after one-decimal rounding tolerance. AUC coordinates agree with historical inventory values rounded to six decimals.
assets.limitations: The historical AUC points mix fp16 rectangle-arm probes with fp32 shaped/coverage probes. The vector extraction verifies retained summary-to-mark agreement, not generation of raw masks or validity of the interpretation. Full raster numeric-label reading is not certified: some labels overlap.
assets.unresolved_scientific_claim: The title's general statement that masking anatomy more accurately does not help, and any significance/non-separation claim inferred from a point plot with no intervals.
assets.minimal_action: Parent may regenerate from the exact Table2 seed42 hidden_pct_on_anat fields and explicitly chosen matched-epoch, matched-precision AUC inventory rows. Use a descriptive title, exactly five arms, defined target-union purity, and clear no-retraining/no-causal-ranking limits. Otherwise remove the scatter and point readers to the verified geometry and performance tables.

assets.caption:
Window occlusion ($W{=}7$) amplifies the same signal roughly sevenfold
and suppresses single-volume noise. For mean-pooled models, single-slice
occlusion systematically under-estimates attributed signal; the windowed variant
recovers more signal. As in Figure~\ref{fig:interp-slice}, each probe
contributes a glaucoma mean (solid) and a healthy mean (dashed) with no interval
drawn, and the curve stops where a full window no longer fits.
ocr_text: Amplifies single-slice signal 7x while smoothing noise
Window-center slice position along 200-slice volume axis
assets.classification: Six quantitative class-mean attribution curves, sample counts, and an empirical sevenfold-amplification title.
assets.rationale: The actual image title says it amplifies single-slice signal 7x while smoothing noise. The asset equals the retained summary PNG, but no window_contrib arrays or independently extracted vector series were recovered. Window size seven is protocol; sevenfold gain is an empirical claim, not the same kind of number.
assets.limitations: Historical documentation asserts the same conclusion but is not independent numeric evidence. Even disclosure that arrays are unavailable does not verify displayed curves, means, counts, amplification, or noise reduction.
assets.unresolved_scientific_claim: Sevenfold amplification, systematic underestimation by single-slice occlusion, and improved signal/noise or completeness.
assets.minimal_action: Remove this figure and its empirical comparison unless original window/slice summary arrays can be retained and independently checked. A non-results method description may state that zeroing a contiguous window is a different perturbation; do not claim a recovered gain or smoothing effect.

assets.caption:
The two-peak structure is consistent with an orientation mixture;
OD/OS labels are unavailable for confirmation. Clustering
per-volume attribution curves into two groups returns near-perfect mirror images
of one another for the two well-structured probes, which is what laterality
flipping would produce, rather than
bilateral anatomy; the \textsc{d1} row does not show that structure. Glaucoma
volumes only, cluster $n$ in each legend, no interval drawn, and the $y$ range
differs by row.
ocr_text: OD/OS mixing hypothesis: clustering on per-volume slice-contribution curves (glaucoma class only)
If mixing were real, cluster means would be mirror-images -4 right column should show two curves on top of each other.
assets.classification: Six quantitative cluster-mean line panels with correlations and cluster sample counts.
assets.rationale: Actual labels include mirrored correlations +0.971, +0.988 and +0.237, with distinct raw correlations and cluster sizes. The retained code describes L2 normalization, k-means with two clusters, and reversal of cluster-mean curves; arrays needed to validate those results are absent.
assets.limitations: No ground-truth eye-laterality labels exist in the described evidence. Mirror similarity cannot establish actual OD/OS storage reversal; clustering and flipping are model-derived, not external validation. A historical PNG/code match cannot reproduce correlations.
assets.unresolved_scientific_claim: Near-perfect mirror structure of two probes, the population-mixture explanation, and identification of that mixture as OD/OS.
assets.minimal_action: Remove empirical OD/OS and mirror-clustering findings without retained attribution summaries. It is defensible to keep only a methodological caution that averaging over unknown orientations can obscure interpretation, without claiming the phenomenon was demonstrated in these data.

Per-patch occlusion heat maps on individual B-scans, drawn on a shared
scale with the slice mean subtracted so that maps are comparable across volumes.
Attribution is broadly distributed

patch level. These are hand-picked illustrative volumes rather than a sample,
the overlay is the patch grid rendered with smoothing and so carries no detail
finer than a patch, and no colour bar is drawn, so the maps show sign and
spatial pattern but no readable magnitude.

assets.classification: Selected historical B-scan overlays with empirical probabilities and signed slice contributions, plus unverified clinical/descriptive diagnoses.
assets.rationale: The released file is byte-identical to results/summary/heatmap_grid.png, not heatmap_grid_BC.png. Its six row labels match the assembler, including probabilities, signed slice contributions, and 'RNFL thinning visible'/'Localized pathology'. The corresponding producer scales each overlay by its own max absolute delta with interpolation; the separately retained B+C figure is the shared-scale/mean-subtracted alternative. The current caption misidentifies that transformation.
assets.limitations: The exact historical execution and per-patch arrays are unretained. Code correspondence and identity establish a documented variant discrepancy, not an independent rerun. No colorbar means no readable magnitude; normalization cannot be recovered uniquely from blended RGB pixels. Clinical labels have not been independently reviewed.
assets.unresolved_scientific_claim: Shared normalization and mean subtraction in this specific figure; broadly distributed attribution or stronger slice-than-patch agreement inferred from selected images; printed patient-level model predictions/contributions and clinical interpretations.
assets.minimal_action: Prefer omitting this grid and any main-text claim resting on it. Conditional illustration-only retention requires removing unsupported quantitative/clinical headings and describing selected historical, interpolated, per-image-normalized overlays without cross-case magnitude, disease-localization, coverage, policy-mechanism, or representativeness claims. Review the resulting exact asset and corrected caption anew; this is not approval of the current asset.

assets.caption:
Attribution stratified by TP / FN / TN / FP. Errors reproduce the
correct pattern at lower amplitude rather than selecting different anatomy.
Curves are per-outcome means with the $n$ in each legend; panels share a
$y$ range and no interval is drawn.
ocr_text: Attribution stratified by prediction outcome — TP vs FN, TN vs FP
(do correct predictions look at different slices than wrong ones?)
assets.classification: Twelve outcome-mean attribution curves across three panels, with empirical accuracies and outcome counts.
assets.rationale: Actual figure headings include accuracy percentages; legends include TP/FN/TN/FP counts. The image is not a qualitative anatomy illustration. No matching attribution/probability arrays or retained mean-series tables are available for curve or stratification validation.
assets.limitations: Outcome labels/counts in the PNG or prose do not validate the plotted means. No uncertainty is shown. Descriptive mean-shape similarity cannot establish the anatomical cause of errors.
assets.unresolved_scientific_claim: Errors preserve the correct anatomical pattern at lower amplitude, confidence-invariant attribution, and error-rate association with attribution amplitude.
assets.minimal_action: Remove this result and its empirical error-pattern interpretation unless the original stratified summary arrays and threshold definition can be validated. Do not substitute frozen-policy probe data for these fine-tuned models.

assets.caption:
Single-slice occlusion attribution against native slice position, for
all three fine-tuned probes. Each probe contributes two curves, a mean over the
glaucoma volumes (solid) and a mean over the healthy volumes (dashed), with
each $n$ in the legend and no interval drawn.
Despite spanning zero to 7.14M probe parameters they converge on the same
structure. The $y$-axis is
\emph{signed} $\Delta$logit: peaks are slices whose removal lowers the logit,
the central dip is slices whose removal raises it, and only slices near zero are
genuinely unused.

assets.classification: Six class-mean signed attribution curves with sample counts and a native-position/subset-index axis mapping.
assets.rationale: Actual labels give three fine-tuned probes, glaucoma n=1466 and healthy n=1534, and a 64-slice subset relabeling of a 200-position native axis. No retained per-volume or mean-series arrays support independent verification of the visible curve values.
assets.limitations: Near-zero signed population means can arise from cancellation, not genuinely unused slices. A shared curve envelope is not causal anatomy evidence or validation of frozen-policy AUC rankings. The 7.14M manuscript versus 7.17M documentation counts are configuration-dependent and are not resolved or overwritten here.
assets.unresolved_scientific_claim: Cross-probe convergence of attribution structure, diffuse middle-volume use, and the assertion that near-zero means imply unused slices.
assets.minimal_action: Remove the quantitative result without recoverable series. A methods-only description can define signed delta-logit as baseline minus occluded logit and warn that a near-zero class mean does not prove nonuse. Do not relabel these empirical curves illustrative-only.
